question: What were the two most famous hallmarks of the Garoghlanian tribe to which Aram and Mourad belonged? 🏕️
explanation: Brilliant! Despite being extremely poor, the Garoghlanian family was famous for their absolute honesty and trust; it was unimaginable that any member of the tribe would be a thief. 🌟
hint: Think about the moral values that prevented them from keeping the stolen horse permanently.

question: How old was the narrator, Aram, when the events of the story took place? 👦
explanation: Spot on! Aram was nine years old when he experienced this magical summer, viewing the world through the innocent and imaginative eyes of childhood. 🌈
hint: He was four years younger than his cousin Mourad.

question: How old was Aram's cousin, Mourad? 🧑
explanation: Perfect! Mourad was thirteen years old, and he was considered the crazy member of the family by almost everyone who knew him. 🐎
hint: He was a teenager, four years older than Aram.

question: At what time of day did Mourad wake Aram by tapping on the window? ⏰
explanation: Awesome! Mourad tapped on Aram's window at four in the morning, when it was still dark but light enough to see what was outside. 🌙
hint: It was very early, long before the sun fully rose.

question: What did Aram see when he looked out of his window? 🪟
explanation: Excellent! Aram saw Mourad sitting gracefully on a magnificent, beautiful white horse, which seemed like a dream to him. ✨
hint: It is the central animal mentioned in the title of the story.

question: Why did Aram find it difficult to believe that Mourad owned the horse? 🏚️
options: The Garoghlanian tribe was incredibly poor 🪙
Mourad did not know how to ride 🏇
The horse was a wild animal 🐺
answer: The Garoghlanian tribe was incredibly poor 🪙
explanation: Great job! Aram knew they were poverty-stricken and didn't even have enough money for food, so buying such a magnificent horse was impossible. 🛖
hint: Think about the financial situation of the Garoghlanian family.

question: How did Mourad justify taking the horse without permission? 🤔
options: He said the owner was cruel 😠
He claimed he found it in the woods 🌲
He believed stealing a horse for a ride wasn't stealing unless they offered to sell it 💬
He said it was a gift from Uncle Khosrove 🎁
answer: He believed stealing a horse for a ride wasn't stealing unless they offered to sell it 💬
explanation: Brilliant! In his innocent and twisted logic, Mourad convinced himself that taking the horse just to ride it out of passion wasn't the same as stealing for money. 🧠
hint: He drew a line between enjoying a ride and selling the animal for profit.

question: Who was considered the 'natural descendant of the crazy streak' in the tribe before Mourad? 🧔
explanation: Spot on! Mourad was considered the natural successor to the eccentric and unpredictable Uncle Khosrove, who was famous for his massive temper. 🌋
hint: He is the large man with the biggest mustache in the valley.

question: What was Uncle Khosrove's famous catchphrase for every problem? 📢
options: It is no harm; pay no attention to it. ✋
answer: It is no harm; pay no attention to it. ✋
explanation: Perfect! Uncle Khosrove was a man of furious temper and would roar this exact phrase to dismiss any problem, no matter how serious it was. 🌪️
hint: He tells people to ignore the issue because it doesn't matter.

question: What news did Arak bring to his father, Uncle Khosrove, at the barber shop? 🔥
explanation: Awesome! Even when his own son ran eight blocks to tell him their house was burning, Khosrove simply roared his usual catchphrase to pay no attention to it! ✂️
hint: It was a major emergency involving flames and their home.

question: Where did Aram live in the town? 🏘️
options: At the edge of town, on Walnut Avenue 🛣️
answer: At the edge of town, on Walnut Avenue 🛣️
explanation: Excellent! Aram lived at the very edge of the town on Walnut Avenue, beyond which lay the open country with vineyards and orchards. 🍇
hint: It was a street named after a type of nut.

question: What word did Mourad shout to make the horse run during his solo ride? 🐎
explanation: Great job! Mourad kicked his heels into the horse and shouted 'Vazire, run!' to command the horse into a furious sprint. 🌪️
hint: It sounds like the title of a royal advisor in ancient courts.

question: What happened to Aram when it was his turn to ride the horse alone? 🤕
options: He rode it perfectly like a jockey 🏆
The horse ran into the vineyard and he fell off 🍇
He got lost in the woods 🌲
answer: The horse ran into the vineyard and he fell off 🍇
explanation: Brilliant! The horse didn't listen to Aram; it leaped over seven vines in the vineyard, throwing Aram to the ground before running away. 🍂
hint: He lost control and ended up on the dirt.

question: How long did it take Mourad to find the runaway horse after Aram fell? ⏱️
explanation: Spot on! Mourad ran down the road and it took him about half an hour to track down the horse and bring it back. 🏃‍♂️
hint: It was exactly thirty minutes.

question: Where did the boys decide to hide the horse during the day? 🛖
explanation: Perfect! They took the horse to the barn of a deserted vineyard, which was the perfect quiet spot to keep it hidden from the townspeople. 🌾
hint: It was an old farm that no longer grew grapes actively.

question: Who was the original owner of the deserted vineyard where they hid the horse? 👨‍🌾
explanation: Awesome! The deserted vineyard had once been the pride of a farmer named Fetvajian, but it was now empty and perfect for hiding a horse. 🏚️
hint: The name starts with the letter 'F'.

question: What did the boys feed the horse while it was hidden in the barn? 🌾
explanation: Excellent! The old barn had some oats and dry alfalfa, which provided good nourishment for the beautiful white horse. 🐎
hint: It is standard, dry horse feed.

question: Who was the actual, rightful owner of the beautiful white horse? 🧔
explanation: Great job! The horse belonged to John Byro, an Assyrian farmer who visited Aram's house to complain about his stolen animal. 🐴
hint: He is the farmer who eventually encounters the boys with his horse.

question: What was John Byro's nationality/ethnicity? 🌍
explanation: Brilliant! John Byro was an Assyrian farmer who learned to speak Armenian out of loneliness so he could communicate with his neighbors. 🤝
hint: It is an ancient Middle Eastern ethnicity starting with 'A'.

question: How much money did John Byro say he had paid for the white horse? 💵
explanation: Spot on! He lamented to Aram's mother and Uncle Khosrove that the horse had cost him sixty dollars, a large sum of money at that time. 🪙
hint: It is three times twenty.

question: Why was John Byro's surrey (carriage) useless to him? 🛺
options: He had no horse to pull it 🐎
It was too small for him 📦
answer: He had no horse to pull it 🐎
explanation: Perfect! A surrey is a horse-drawn carriage. Without his beautiful white horse, his surrey was completely useless. 🛑
hint: A carriage needs an animal to move it.

question: How far did John Byro have to walk to visit Aram's house? 🚶‍♂️
explanation: Awesome! Because his horse was stolen, John Byro had to walk ten miles, which caused his left leg to pain him greatly. 🤕
hint: It is a double-digit number.

question: What did Aram ask Mourad to promise after John Byro visited? 🙏
options: To return the horse the next day 🌅
Not to return the horse until Aram learned to ride 🏇
To buy a saddle for the horse 🪢
answer: Not to return the horse until Aram learned to ride 🏇
explanation: Excellent! Aram was thrilled about the horse and selfishly begged Mourad not to return it until he, too, could ride perfectly. ✨
hint: Aram wanted more time to master a specific skill.

question: How long did Aram think it would take him to learn to ride the horse? ⏳
explanation: Great job! Aram estimated it would take him a full year to learn to ride, to which Mourad replied that they couldn't keep a horse that long! ⏱️
hint: It is the equivalent of 365 days.

question: What was the maximum time limit Mourad set before they had to return the horse? ⏱️
explanation: Brilliant! Mourad stated that they must return the horse to its true owner in six months at the latest to protect the Garoghlanian honor. 🛡️
hint: It is exactly half a year.

question: What was Mourad doing when Aram ran to tell him about John Byro's visit? 🐦
options: Nursing a young robin with a hurt wing 🩹
answer: Nursing a young robin with a hurt wing 🩹
explanation: Spot on! Mourad was sitting under a peach tree, tenderly trying to heal the wing of a young robin, showing his deep connection with nature. 🌱
hint: He was helping a small, injured bird.

question: What phrase did Mourad frequently use to show his confidence in handling different situations? 😎
explanation: Perfect! Mourad confidently claimed 'I have a way with horses', 'a way with dogs', and 'a way with farmers' to assure Aram that everything was under control. 🌟
hint: He claims to have a special 'way' of dealing with things.

question: According to Aram's realization, how long had Mourad been riding the horse before inviting Aram? 🕵️‍♂️
explanation: Awesome! Aram figured out that Mourad had already been taking early morning rides for a month before he finally tapped on Aram's window. 🐎
hint: It was the same length of time John Byro said the horse had been missing.

question: Who did the boys run into while taking the horse to the deserted vineyard one morning? 🚶‍♂️
explanation: Excellent! In a moment of great suspense, they literally bumped into the true owner, John Byro, who was on his way to town. 😲
hint: They met the man who was missing the exact horse they were leading.

question: What did John Byro do when he saw the boys with the white horse? 👁️
options: He yelled at them for stealing 😡
explanation: Great job! Instead of jumping to accusations, John Byro politely said 'Good morning' and studied the horse very closely. 🔍
hint: He examined the animal with intense focus.

question: What specific part of the horse did John Byro ask to examine? 🦷
explanation: Brilliant! To confirm his suspicions, John Byro looked into the horse's mouth and noted, 'Tooth for tooth,' realizing it was identical to his own horse. 🦷
hint: He checked the inside of its mouth.

question: What conclusion did John Byro make out loud after inspecting the horse's teeth? 👯
options: It is the twin of my horse. 🐴🐴
This is a completely different breed. 🦓
I must buy this horse from you. 💵
answer: It is the twin of my horse. 🐴🐴
explanation: Spot on! Because he trusted the honesty of the boys' family, he chose to believe his eyes were deceiving him and called it a 'twin'. 🌟
hint: He decided it looked exactly like his horse but couldn't possibly be his.

question: Why did John Byro refuse to believe that Mourad and Aram had stolen his horse? 🛡️
options: Because they were too small to ride 👦
Because of the Garoghlanian family's fame for honesty 🤝
Because Mourad lied to him convincingly 🤥
answer: Because of the Garoghlanian family's fame for honesty 🤝
explanation: Perfect! The reputation of the Garoghlanian tribe was so strong that John Byro trusted their heritage more than his own eyes. 🏆
hint: Their tribe's hallmark protected them from being accused.

question: What did the boys do early the very next morning after meeting John Byro? 🌅
options: They sold the horse in the market 💰
They took the horse to John Byro's vineyard and left it there 🍇
They rode the horse to another city 🗺️
They hid the horse in a cave 🦇
answer: They took the horse to John Byro's vineyard and left it there 🍇
explanation: Awesome! Guilt-ridden and eager to uphold their family's honor, they quietly returned the horse to its rightful owner the next morning. 🐴
hint: They put the horse back where it belonged.

question: What animals followed the boys silently when they returned the horse to John Byro's vineyard? 🐕
explanation: Excellent! Some farm dogs followed them around in the vineyard, but miraculously, they didn't make a single sound. 🐾
hint: They are common farm animals that usually bark at strangers.

question: Why didn't the dogs bark at the boys? 🤫
explanation: Great job! Just like with the horse and the farmer, Mourad's deep understanding of animals kept the dogs completely calm and silent. 🐕
hint: Mourad used his special 'claim' about understanding animals.

question: How did Mourad say goodbye to the horse before leaving John Byro's vineyard? 🐴
options: He pressed his nose into the horse's nose and patted it ❤️
answer: He pressed his nose into the horse's nose and patted it ❤️
explanation: Brilliant! Mourad showed his deep affection for the animal by pressing his nose against its nose and giving it a gentle pat before walking away. 🥰
hint: It was a very close, affectionate physical gesture.

question: When John Byro brought his surrey to Aram's house that afternoon, what did he say about the returned horse? 💪
explanation: Spot on! Mourad's excellent care and riding had actually improved the horse; it was now stronger and had a much better temper! 🏇
hint: The horse benefited from Mourad's care.

question: How did Uncle Khosrove react to John Byro's good news about the returned horse? 🗣️
options: He roared, 'Quiet, man, quiet. Your horse has been returned. Pay no attention to it.' 🌋
He demanded a reward from John Byro 💰
answer: He roared, 'Quiet, man, quiet. Your horse has been returned. Pay no attention to it.' 🌋
explanation: Perfect! True to his character, Uncle Khosrove became irritated and shouted his famous catchphrase, dismissing the farmer's joy entirely. 🛑
hint: He used his classic, dismissive catchphrase.

question: What does the beautiful white horse symbolize for the narrator, Aram? 🌈
options: The magnificent and magical dreams of childhood ✨
answer: The magnificent and magical dreams of childhood ✨
explanation: Awesome! To Aram, the horse wasn't stolen property; it was the embodiment of his wildest childhood dreams and longing for adventure. 🌟
hint: Think about innocence, wonder, and the magic of youth.

question: Who is the author of 'The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse'? ✍️
explanation: Excellent! William Saroyan is the acclaimed author of this beautiful, nostalgic story about Armenian-American life. 📖
hint: His first name is William.

question: What is the primary setting of the story? 🗺️
explanation: Great job! The story is set in the rural San Joaquin Valley in California, where many Armenian immigrants settled and farmed. 🍇
hint: It is a famous agricultural valley in California.

question: What did Aram feel when he first saw the horse outside his window? 😲
options: A mixture of delight and fear ✨
answer: A mixture of delight and fear ✨
explanation: Brilliant! Aram was thrilled by the breathtaking beauty of the horse (delight) but also scared because he knew Mourad must have stolen it (fear). 🎢
hint: He felt two contrasting emotions at the exact same time.

question: According to the story, what was more important to the Garoghlanian tribe than money? 🛡️
options: Pride, honesty, and right from wrong ⚖️
answer: Pride, honesty, and right from wrong ⚖️
explanation: Spot on! They were proud first, honest next, and believed strongly in doing the right thing, which defined their entire identity. 🏆
hint: It involves their moral compass and reputation.

question: Why did Aram run down the stairs and leap into the yard when Mourad invited him? 🏃‍♂️
explanation: Perfect! Driven by his ultimate childhood dream, Aram didn't hesitate to join his cousin for a magical morning ride. 🏇
hint: He couldn't resist the temptation waiting outside.

question: Which of these words best describes Mourad's character? 🌪️
explanation: Awesome! Mourad lived life on his own terms, deeply connected to nature, making him seem 'crazy' to the rest of the logical world. 🍃
hint: He is compared to Uncle Khosrove for a reason.

question: What time of year does the story take place? ☀️
explanation: Excellent! As the title suggests, this unforgettable childhood memory occurred during the warm, bright days of summer. 🌻
hint: Look at the title of the chapter!

question: How did Aram and Mourad communicate when they were trying not to be heard in the early morning? 🤫
explanation: Great job! Being of Armenian descent, the boys communicated quietly in their native tongue as they sneaked away for their ride. 🤫
hint: They used their family's native language.

question: What made John Byro's visit to Aram's house particularly tense for Aram? 😬
options: Aram knew John Byro was talking about the horse Mourad had hidden 🐎
answer: Aram knew John Byro was talking about the horse Mourad had hidden 🐎
explanation: Brilliant! Aram realized that the 'stolen' horse John Byro was crying about was the exact same horse he had been riding that morning! 😲
hint: Aram had a guilty secret related to the farmer's complaint.

question: What is the ultimate theme explored in 'The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse'? 📖
options: The innocence of childhood colliding with moral boundaries 🌟
The history of agriculture in California 🚜
answer: The innocence of childhood colliding with moral boundaries 🌟
explanation: Spot on! The story beautifully captures how the innocence and passion of youth (Mourad and Aram) navigate the complex adult world of morality, honesty, and right vs. wrong. ⚖️
hint: It deals with growing up and learning the difference between right and wrong.
